summary:
All six owed rows are met, and 13 of the design's 14 criteria are met. The slice does not pass cleanly because of criterion 13 (the window stays responsive). On the real D:\ drive it broke the design's own bars in 1 of 6 runs at the default window size.

**What I ran:**
- Build: clean. Core tests: 240/240. Fitness: all 43 rules hold. I published the exe fresh from HEAD 3dbaedf.
- The project's cases: WindowCases -Case All passed all 34 (643 s); HookCases and RuleCases C-001 passed too. T-003 opens the 100k folder in 97.8 / 3.2 / 2.5 / 2.5 / 2.2 ms (135.6 ms cold in a work-area-tall window). T-004's WeakReference showed the first store released both while the second scan ran and after it ended. T-005 passed: longest wait 63 ms.

**Real data, beyond the project's cases:**
- **Real folder (the 780 MB repo-local .NET SDK):** I compared all 249 rows, read to depth 3, against Get-ChildItem. Sizes matched exactly, every folder's children were largest first, all 248 shares matched a hand calculation, and child counts matched the listing.
- **D:\ chosen as a drive root (527,495 files, 2.3 s scan):** Finished, with the tree rooted at D:\. All 15 top-level sizes matched Get-ChildItem, the root equals the sum of its rows, and all 70 shares and bars match. 2 unreadable folders show 'could not be opened' and 2 links show 'link, not followed'.
- **C:\ chosen as a drive root (3,597,756 files, 830,964 folders, 20,003 links):** Finished after 1,299 s with the tree shown rooted at C:\. Peak private memory was 731 MiB, under the 1 GiB budget.
- **A hardlinked pair read through the tree (design criterion 14, which no window case reads from the tree):** counted once. The root is 196 KB and the second name shows 0 bytes.

**The criterion-13 finding:** I ran T-005's scenario (move and resize during a scan, then a rescan) on D:\ 9 times.
- One of the 6 runs at the default 860 px height broke both bars: the rescan's longest wait was 1,318.5 ms (bar 1 s), and the scan phase's 95th percentile was 368.5 ms over 28 probes (bar 200 ms).
- In every other run the rescan phase peaked at 658–768 ms. In all 9 runs the first move after the second scan started took 476–649 ms, and at the old 620 px height the rescan still peaked at 740–768 ms. So the slow move is not caused by the taller window.
- It matches the window-move stall build-slice already recorded as belonging to SL-039/SL-040's window. The scan phase has the same kind of stall before any tree exists. I did not measure whether the pre-slice exe also goes over 1 s.
- Owed row 6's own check still holds: the longest wait in any run was 1.32 s, far from the 5 s after which Windows marks a window 'Not Responding'.

**Obligations:**
- O-014 (owed here) is discharged. T-004 passed, and on real D:\ the first store was released with a row selected and a folder open, both during and after the second scan.
- O-031 (owed to build-slice) is still open. MainWindow.xaml.cs:62 and :107-113 still use SystemParameters.WorkArea. This machine's second monitor sits beside the primary at the same height, so neither failing layout can happen here.

**Other observations:**
- When the unreadable-folders expander shows (on D:\ and C:\), the largest-files list shrinks to 56 px with 2 full rows, a side effect of this slice's 1:3 split.
- The full C:\ scan took 21.6 minutes. The project constraint allows 'a few minutes' for a big drive; that is a scanner matter, not this slice's.

I wrote only build output and a scratch folder under %TEMP%, which I deleted. Git status is unchanged.

criteria.criterion: 1. show the tree when a scan completes (row 1)
criteria.how: T-001/C-002/T-004 endings show FolderTree with one root row, headings, and no list. Real drives: D:\ and C:\ picked as drive roots finish with the tree rooted at D:\ and C:\ (14 full rows in view).

criteria.criterion: 2. order a folder's children largest first (row 2)
criteria.how: T-001 shows dense.bin above sparse.bin, which is larger in bytes but takes 64 KiB on disk. On real data every opened parent was non-increasing by on disk: 18 parents in .dotnet and all parents in the D:\ walk.
T-001 deep\mid\low, chain and root. On real data all 249 .dotnet rows and all 15 D:\ top-level rows equal Get-ChildItem sums exactly, and each root equals the sum of its rows.

criteria.criterion: 4. show a folder with nothing readable in it (row 4)
criteria.how: T-001 'empty' has no expander and 0 bytes. B-007: 12 denied folders show 'could not be opened'. Real D:\: 2 folders show 'could not be opened' with no expander. The 'could not be read in full' branch was not exercised.
T-001: j, sd and sf show 0 bytes and 'link, not followed', with no expander. Real D:\: 2 rows show 'link, not followed'.

criteria.criterion: 6. show a share of a zero parent (row 3)
criteria.how: T-001 zeros\z1-3 draw '0.0 %' with a 0 px bar. Temp tree only, not checked on real data.

criteria.criterion: 7. format a share to one decimal (row 3)
criteria.how: T-001 thirds, twothirds, sixteenths (6.3 / 93.8 %) and tiny (0.0 % with a 1 px bar). On real data, 248 .dotnet shares and 70 D:\ shares match the hand calculation, with midpoints rounded away from zero.
T-001's rendered NameText shows 'size_&_order', 'my_file&co.bin' and a 149-character name exactly, on a 20 px row.
T-003 in my run: 97.8 / 3.2 / 2.5 / 2.5 / 2.2 ms at the default size, and 135.6 ms at most in a work-area-tall window; only 29 or 46 rows built.

criteria.criterion: 10. keep expand state through recycling and re-expansion (row 2)
criteria.how: T-002 passed in my run: only f02 is open, by the node and as drawn, and order and sizes are unchanged after scrolling and reopening.

criteria.criterion: 11. start a second scan while a tree is shown (rows 1 and 6)
criteria.how: T-004 passed, and the same check on real D:\ with a folder open and a depth-2 row selected: the first store was collectable during the second scan and after it; the second ending shows the new tree.

criteria.criterion: 12. end a scan without a tree (row 1)
criteria.how: T-006 passed: Stop leaves the list showing and no tree; a fault exits 70 with the tree empty; a missing root reads 'Could not read' with no tree.

criteria.criterion: 13. keep the window responsive during a scan (row 6)
criteria.how: T-005 passed on its temp tree (max 63 ms). On real D:\, 1 of 6 runs at the default size broke both of the design's bars: rescan max 1,318.5 ms (bar 1 s) and scan p95 368.5 ms over 28 probes (bar 200 ms). The rescan's first move stalls 476–649 ms in every run, at 620 px as well, which fits the pre-existing SL-039/SL-040 window-move stall that build-slice recorded. No run came near the 5 s after which Windows marks a window 'Not Responding'.

criteria.criterion: 14. count a hardlinked file in the tree
criteria.how: My hook run on a temp tree with a hardlinked pair in different folders: the root is 196 KB, charged once; the second name and its folder show 0 bytes and 0.0 %.

planned.evidence: Temp trees: T-001, C-002 and T-004 show the root row and its children at a Finished ending. Real: D:\ and C:\ launched as drive roots end 'Finished' with FolderTree visible and rooted there; the D:\ tree was read to depth 2 (71 rows drawn). Every run entered through the launch argument or the window's own StartScan, which the drive buttons and Choose folder call. The folder dialog itself was not driven.

The order of every expanded folder matches the expected order: T-001 over every folder to depth 4, including the sparse/dense case where byte order and on-disk order differ. Real data: all 18 opened .dotnet parents and every D:\ parent are non-increasing by on disk.

The drawn percentages equal hand-computed shares at one decimal: T-001 checks thirds, sixteenths, tiny and zeros, and I checked 248 .dotnet rows and 70 D:\ rows on real data. Bars are drawn at share×60 px, 1 px minimum for a nonzero share, 0 for a zero share.

T-001: deep\mid\low (three levels deep) and the root show the expected totals. Real: all 249 .dotnet rows and all 15 top-level D:\ rows equal Get-ChildItem sums to the byte, and each root equals the sum of its rows.

T-003 measured and recorded 5 opens of a 100,000-file folder, from IsExpanded to the first ContextIdle with the first child's container: 97.8 / 3.2 / 2.5 / 2.5 / 2.2 ms at the default size, and 135.6 / 5.3 / 10.5 / 3.4 / 3.5 ms at work-area height. All are under 500 ms.

The window was moved and resized during scans on a temp tree (T-005: max wait 63 ms) and 9 times on real D:\. The worst UI-thread wait was 1.32 s, far below the 5 s after which Windows marks a window 'Not Responding'. I did not see the 'Not Responding' state itself; this conclusion rests on the measured waits. The design's stricter 1 s bar was broken once (criterion 13).

obligations.evidence: The precondition that the old store is released before the next scan builds another holds. T-004 in my full run: with a 3,000-row folder open and a depth-3 row selected and focused, released=true while the second scan ran (scanning=true, tree=false) and again after it ended. Repeated on real D:\ with a folder open and a depth-2 row selected: released=true both times. In the code, StartScan sets _result and LastResult to null and closes the FolderTreeSession before Scanner.Scan starts (MainWindow.xaml.cs:194-199, 392-400).

Still open; owed to build-slice. MainWindow.xaml.cs:62 (height clamp) and :107-113 (OnSourceInitialized move-up) still compare against SystemParameters.WorkArea, the primary monitor's work area. I could not reproduce the failure here: this machine's second monitor (DISPLAY5, X=-1920 Y=0, 1920x1080) sits beside the primary at the same height, so neither the stacked-below nor the offset-lower layout exists.

not_reached: The native folder dialog and a real click on a drive button were never driven. Every run entered through the launch argument or the window's StartScan, which both of those call.

Tree rows on the full C:\ drive (about 4.45M entries) were never read: the hook's fixed 120 s ending deadline is shorter than the 1,299 s scan. Drilling down, opening a 100k folder, and memory growth past the root on a drive that size were not measured. Only the report-mode peak was: 731 MiB with the root opened.

Whether the pre-slice exe (de51999) also passes 1 s on the real D:\ move-and-resize scenario was not measured. That the 1,318 ms stall is SL-039/SL-040's rests on the same slow first move appearing at 620 px and in the scan phase before any tree exists.
The 'Not Responding' state itself was not seen. The conclusion for row 6 rests on measured UI-thread waits (1.32 s at most) against Windows' 5 s hung-window threshold.
O-031's multi-monitor layouts (a monitor below the primary, or one beside it and set lower) do not exist on this machine.
N-001..N-004, the StallRig network cases, were not run: they change SMB client mappings and are person-run.
The 'could not be read in full' row, for a folder whose listing failed partway, was not exercised; an ordinary user cannot make that happen on a real tree.
Only 100% DPI on 1920x1080 monitors was tested. Expanders were opened by setting IsExpanded on the container, not by a real mouse click or keyboard arrow.

When the unreadable-folders expander shows (D:\ and C:\), the largest-files list shrinks to 56 px with 2 full rows, a side effect of this slice's 1:3 split. Nobody has judged whether that is acceptable for SL-040's list.
